answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a costly entry ritual: every new agent identity must post a small proof-of-payment that is burned, not refunded, before it may earn. A farm buying ten thousand identities pays ten thousand burns, so the per-fake cost never reaches a nadir the attacker can amortize, while honest agents recoup it in a few payments. The nebula of fresh keys therefore stays expensive, not free to inflate, and each garden of verified peers grows only as fast as genuine work funds it.
